Que.q: Q1 : What is HTML?
Que.a: HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language. It is a language of World Wide Web. It is a standard text formatting language which is used to create and display pages on the Web. It makes the text more interactive and dynamic. It can turn text into images, tables, links.

Que.q: Q2 : What are Tags?
Que.a: HTML tags are composed of three things: an opening tag, content and ending tag. Some tags are unclosed tags.

Que.simple_text: When a web browser reads an HTML document, the browser reads it from top to bottom and left to right. HTML tags are used to create HTML documents and render their properties. Each HTML tags have different properties.

Que.q: Q6 : Which HTML tag is used to display the data in the tabular form?
Que.a: The HTML table tag is used to display data in tabular form (row * column). It also manages the layout of the page, e.g., header section, navigation bar, body content, footer section. Here is the list of tags used while displaying the data in the tabular form:

row.col: <table>
It defines a table.
<tr>
It defines a row in a table.
<th>
It defines a header cell in a table.
<td>
It defines a cell in a table.
<caption>
It defines the table caption.
<colgroup>
It specifies a group of one or more columns in a table for formatting.
<col>
It is used with <colgroup> element to specify column properties for each column.
<tbody>
It is used to group the body content in a table.
<thead>
It is used to group the header content in a table.
<tfooter>
It is used to group the footer content in a table.

Que.q: Q7 : What are some common lists that are used when designing a page?
Que.a: There are many common lists which are used to design a page. You can choose any or a combination of the following list types:

list.Ordered list: The ordered list displays elements in numbered format. It is represented by <ol> tag.
list.Unordered list: The unordered list displays elements in bulleted format. It is represented by <ul> tag.
list.Definition list: The definition list displays elements in definition form like in dictionary. The <dl>, <dt> and <dd> tags are used to define description list.

Que.q: Q8 : What is the difference between the ‘id’ attribute and the ‘class’ attribute of HTML elements?
Que.a: Multiple elements in HTML can have the same class value, whereas a value of id attribute of one element cannot be associated with another HTML element.

Que.q: Q9 : What is semantic HTML?
Que.a: Semantic HTML is a coding style. It is the use of HTML markup to reinforce the semantics or meaning of the content. For example: In semantic HTML tag is not used for bold statement as well as tag is used for italic. Instead of these we use and tags.

Que.q: Q10 : Describe HTML layout structure?
Que.a: Every web page has different components to display the intended content and a specific UI. But still, there are few things which are templated and are globally accepted way to structure the web page, such as:

list.<header>: Stores the starting information about the web page.
list.<footer>: Represents the last section of the page.
list.<nav>: The navigation menu of the HTML page.
list.<article>: It is a set of information.
list.<section>: It is used inside the article block to define the basic structure of a page.

Que.q: Q11 : How to optimize website assets loading?
Que.a: To optimize website load time we need to optimize its asset loading and for that:

list.CDN hosting: A CDN or content delivery network is geographically distributed servers to help reduce latency.
list.File compression: This is a method that helps to reduce the size of an asset to reduce the data transfer.
list.File concatenation: This reduces the number of HTTP calls.
list.Minify scripts: This reduces the overall file size of js and CSS files.
list.Parallel downloads: Hosting assets in multiple subdomains can help to bypass the download limit of 6 assets per domain of all modern browsers. This can be configured but most general users never modify these settings.
list.Lazy Loading: Instead of loading all the assets at once, the non-critical assets can be loaded on a need basis.

Que.q: Q13 : What is the difference between <strong>, <b> tags and <em>, <i> tags?
Que.a: The effect on a normal webpage of the tags <strong>, <b>  and <em>, <i> is the same. <b> and <i> tags stands for bold and italic. These two tags only apply font styling and bold tag <b>, just adds more ink to the text, these tags don't say anything about the text.Whereas, <strong> and <em> tags represent that the span of text is of strong importance or more importance and emphatic stress respectively than the rest of the text. These tags have semantic meaning.

Que.q: Q14 : How is Cell Padding different from Cell Spacing?
Que.a: Cell Spacing is the space or gap between two consecutive cells. Whereas, Cell Padding is the space or gap between the text/ content of the cell and the edge/ border of the cell. Please refer to the above figure example to find the difference.

Que.q: Q15 : How can we club two or more rows or columns into a single row or column in an HTML table?
Que.a: HTML provides two table attributes “rowspan” and “colspan” to make a cell span to multiple rows and columns respectively.

Que.q: Q16 : Is it possible to change an inline element into a block level element?
Que.a: Yes, it is possible using the “display” property with its value as “block”, to change the inline element into a block-level element.

Que.q: Q17 : In how many ways can we position an HTML element? Or what are the permissible values of the position attribute?
Que.a: There are mainly 7 values of position attribute that can be used to position an HTML element:

list.static: Default value. Here the element is positioned according to the normal flow of the document.
list.absolute: Here the element is positioned relative to its parent element. The final position is determined by the values of left, right, top, bottom.
list.fixed: This is similar to absolute except here the elements are positioned relative to the <html> element.
list.relative: Here the element is positioned according to the normal flow of the document and positioned relative to its original/ normal position.
list.initial: This resets the property to its default value.
list.inherit: Here the element inherits or takes the property of its parent.

Que.q: Q18 : What is the difference between “display: none” and “visibility: hidden”, when used as attributes to the HTML element?
Que.a: When we use the attribute “visibility: hidden” for an HTML element then that element will be hidden from the webpage but still takes up space. Whereas, if we use the “display: none” attribute for an HTML element then the element will be hidden, and also it won’t take up any space on the webpage.

Que.q: Q19 : In how many ways you can display HTML elements?

list.inline: Using this we can display any block-level element as an inline element. The height and width attribute values of the element will not affect.
list.block: using this, we can display any inline element as a block-level element.
list.inline-block: This property is similar to inline, except by using the display as inline-block, we can actually format the element using height and width values.
list.flex: It displays the container and element as a flexible structure. It follows flexbox property.
list.inline-flex: It displays the flex container as an inline element while its content follows the flexbox properties.
list.grid: It displays the HTML elements as a grid container.
list.none: Using this property we can hide the HTML element.

Que.q: Q20 : How to specify the link in HTML and explain the target attribute?
Que.a: HTML provides a hyperlink - <a> tag to specify the links in a webpage. The ‘href’ attribute is used to specify the link and the ‘target’ attribute is used to specify, where do we want to open the linked document. The ‘target’ attribute can have the following values:

list._self: This is a default value. It opens the document in the same window or tab as it was clicked.
list._blank: It opens the document in a new window or tab.
list._parent: It opens the document in a parent frame.
list._top: It opens the document in a full-body window.

Que.q: Q21 : In how many ways can we specify the CSS styles for the HTML element?
Que.a: There are three ways in which we can specify the styles for HTML elements:

list.Inline: Here we use the ‘style’ attribute inside the HTML element.
list.Internal: Here we use the <style> tag inside the <head> tag. To apply the style we bind the elements using ‘id’ or ‘class’ attributes.
list.External: Here we use the <link> tag inside <head> tag to reference the CSS file into our HTML code. Again the binding between elements and styles is done using ‘id’ or ‘class’ attributes.

Que.q: Q22 : Difference between link tag <link> and anchor tag <a>?
Que.a: The anchor tag <a> is used to create a hyperlink to another webpage or to a certain part of the webpage and these links are clickable, whereas, link tag <link> defines a link between a document and an external resource and these are not clickable.

Que.q: Q23 : When to use scripts in the head and when to use scripts in the body?
Que.a: If the scripts contain some event-triggered functions or jquery library then we should use them in the head section. If the script writes the content on the page or is not inside a function then it should be placed inside the body section at the bottom. In short, follow below three points:

list.1: Place library scripts or event scripts in the head section.
list.2: Place normal scripts that do not write anything on the page, in the head section until there is any performance issue.
list.3: Place scripts that render something on the web page at the bottom of the body section.

Que.q: Q28 : Is the <datalist> tag and <select> tag same?
Que.a: No. The <datalist> tag and <select> tag are different. In the case of <select> tag a user will have to choose from a list of options, whereas <datalist> when used along with the <input> tag provides a suggestion that the user selects one of the options given or can enter some entirely different value.

Que.q: Q29 : What are Semantic Elements?
Que.a: Semantic elements are those which describe the particular meaning to the browser and the developer. Elements like <form>, <table>, <article>, <figure>, etc., are semantic elements.

Que.q: Q30 : What is the difference between <meter> tag and <progress> tag?
Que.a: <progress> tag should be used when we want to show the completion progress of a task, whereas if we just want a scalar measurement within a known range or fraction value. Also, we can specify multiple extra attributes for <meter> tags like ‘form’, ‘low’, ‘high’, ‘min’, etc.

Que.q: Q31 : Is drag and drop possible using HTML5 and how?
Que.a: Yes, in HTML5 we can drag and drop an element. This can be achieved using the drag and drop-related events to be used with the element which we want to drag and drop.

Que.q: Q32 : Difference between SVG and Canvas HTML5 element?

row.col: SVG is a vector based i.e., composed of shapes.
It is Raster based i.e., composed of pixels.
SVG works better with a larger surface.

Que.q: Q33 : What are the significant goals of the HTML5 specification?
Que.a: These were the target area of the HTML5 specs:

list.1: Introduction of new element tags to better structure the web page such as <header> tag.
list.2: Forming a standard in cross-browser behavior and support for different devices and platforms.
list.3: Backward compatible with the older version HTML web pages.
list.4: Introduction of basic interactive elements without the dependency of plugins such as <video> tag instead of the flash plugin.

Que.q: Q34 : Explain the concept of web storage in HTML5?
Que.a: This web storage helps in storing some of the static data in the local storage of the browser so that we do not need to fetch it from the server every time we need it. There is a size limit based on different browsers. This helps in decreasing the load time and a smooth user experience. There are two types of web storage that are used to store data locally in HTML5:

list.Local Storage: This helps in storing data that will be retained even though the user reopens the browser. It is stored for each webapp on different browsers.
list.Session Storage: This is used for one session only. After the user closes the browser this gets deleted.

Que.q: Q35 : What is new about the relationship between the <header> and <h1> tags in HTML5?
Que.a: As HTML5 was all about better semantics and arrangements of the tags and elements, the <header> tag specifies the header section of the webpage. Unlike in previous version there was one <h1> element for the entire webpage, now this is the header for one section such as <article> or <section>. According to the HTML5 specification, each <header> element must at least have one <h1> tag.

Que.q: Q36 : Explain new input types provided by HTML5 for forms?
Que.a: Following are the significant new data types offered by HTML5:

list.Date: Only select date by using type = 'date'
list.Week: Pick a week by using type = 'week'
list.Month: Only select month by using type = 'month'
list.Time: Only select time by using type = 'time'.
list.Datetime: Combination of date and time by using type = 'datetime'
list.Datetime-local: Combination of  date and time by using type = 'datetime-local.' but ignoring the timezone
list.Email: Accepts one or more email addresses using type = 'email'
list.Number: Accepts a numerical value with additional checks like min and max using type = 'number'
list.Search: Allows searching queries by inputting text using type = 'search'
list.Tel: Allows different phone numbers by using type = 'tel'
list.Placeholder: To display a short hint in the input fields before entering a value using type = 'placeholder'
list.Range: Accepts a numerical value within a specific range using type = 'range'
list.Url: Accepts a web address using type = 'url'

list.<audio>: Used for sounds, audio streams, or music, embed audio content without any additional plug-in.
list.<video>: Used for video streams, embed video content etc.
list.<source>: Used for multiple media resources in media elements, such as audio, video, etc.
list.<embed>: Used for an external application or embedded content.

Que.q: Q38 : What are the server-sent events in HTML5?
Que.a: The events pushed from the webserver to the browsers are called server-sent events. DOM elements can be continuously updated using these events. This has a major advantage over straight-up polling. In polling, there is a lot of overhead since every time it is establishing an HTTP connection and tearing it down whereas, in server-sent events, there is one long-lived HTTP connection. To use a server-sent event, <eventsource> element is used. The src attribute of this element specifies the URL from which sends a data stream having the events.

Que.q: Q39 : What are Web Workers?
Que.a: These are added to bring parallelism and async capability. It runs in the background to do the computationally expensive tasks without yielding to make the page responsive. It is achieved by starting a separate thread for such tasks. These are not meant to perform UI operations. There are three types of web workers:

list.Dedicated Workers: These are workers that are utilized by a single script.
list.Shared Workers: These are workers that are utilized by multiple scripts running in different windows, IFrames, etc.
list.Service Workers: These act as proxy servers between web applications, the browser, and the network. Mostly used for push notifications and sync APIs.

Que.q: Q40 : What is the usage of a novalidate attribute for the form tag that is introduced in HTML5?
Que.a: Its value is a boolean type that indicates whether or not the data being submitted by the form will be validated beforehand. By making this false, forms can be submitted without validation which helps users to resume later also.
